newsitem.title: UK: British Gas rejects Ofgas TransCo controls.
newsitem.headline: British Gas rejects Ofgas TransCo controls.

text.p: British Gas Plc said on Thursday that it has rejected price controls proposed by UK regulator Ofgas for its transmission business, TransCo.
British Gas said in a statement that the proposals were "unjustified and unworkable."

The rejection means that the senior British competition authority, the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) will be asked to conduct an inquiry into the proposals which could take many months to complete.

British Gas deputy chairman Philip Rogerson, who is in charge of regulatory issues for the group, said Ofgas's original proposals made in May were damaging to British Gas's shareholders' interests and "not in the overall interests of gas consumers."

He said concessions made by Ofgas in August remained "unrealistic and unacceptable." Ofgas wanted TransCo to cut charges to gas suppliers by 20 percent in 1997 and then by 6.5 percent below inflation for four years.
British Gas said the controls would not allow it enough money to invest adequately in its infrastructure.

British Gas said the proposals would have cut TransCo's annual cash flow by 400 million stg compared with current levels, and said the business also faces higher costs associated with increased competition.
British Gas said no decision on its future dividend policy can be made until "there is greater clarity following the outcome of the MMC's inquiry into TransCo's prices."

It also criticised Ofgas for refusing to allow it to see consultants' reports on which Ofgas's judgements were based, saying this "seriously hampered the company's understanding of the underlying logic behind Ofgas's conclusions."
